key: Show thyself strong for mighty bliss, O Agni, most excellent be thine effulgent splendours. Make easy to maintain our household lordship, and overcome the might of those who hate us.
s: In a short hymn of kindling and offering, after Agni is hailed as king, the prayer turns homeward; Sāyaṇa, on 5.28.3, reads ‘household lordship’ as the shared work of wife and husband, which Agni is to make well ordered, each bound to the other.
src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on Rig Veda 5.28.3, sa.wikisource (printed edition not named), revision 199496 (2019)

evidence.words: किंच हे अग्ने त्वं “जास्पत्यम् । जा जाया च पतिश्च जायापती । तयोः कर्म जास्पत्यम् । तत् “सुयमं सुष्ठु नियमनोपेतम् । अन्योन्यसंश्लिष्टमित्यर्थः । "सम् “आ “कृणुष्व सम्यक् कुरुष्व ।
evidence.gloss: And, O Agni, you: jāspatyam. Jā is wife; wife and husband are jāyāpatī; the work of the two is jāspatyam. That, suyamam, well provided with restraint (well ordered): the meaning is, joined each to the other. Make it well: do it rightly.

reason: The problem holds: the key verse printed the app text’s slip ‘the Godswith homage’. The first fix, correcting js/texts/rigveda/05.js, was not taken: the app file is generated by .scripts/fetch-texts.js from the cached sacred-texts page (.scripts/.cache/rv-05-028.json, which carries the same slip), so a hand edit would be reverted by the next fetch unless an erratum is added there; adding a word to the Readings text may also move the ten-minute division the plan is pinned to (brief div b606361f14), and editing a live app text needs a release. That is an owner change, flagged here, not one a revise pass should make. No standby exists for day 49, so the second fix is taken: another verse of the same hymn with Sāyaṇa’s comment. 5.28.3 (verse.js ok, [381,3], 30 words, no dash) carries his gloss of jāspatyam as ‘jāyāpatī … tayoḥ karma’, the work of the two, wife and husband, and suyamam as well ordered, ‘anyonyasaṃśliṣṭam’, joined each to the other; Wilson follows (‘preserve in concord the relation of man and wife’). Commentator kept; the Viśvavārā reading on 5.28.1 cannot survive a change of verse, so the reading is his on the new verse. Plain sense: 5.28 is six verses of kindling and offering, and 5.28.2 hails the kindled Agni as King; no four-word run from the key; ‘household lordship’ is the only quotation (two words). 45 words. entry-check ok.
